page.text:
A *real sequence* is a function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, denoted
$(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$. Sequences provide the foundational discrete
stepping stones through which the continuous topology of $\mathbb{R}$ is
probed.

Convergence, Cauchy criteria, and infinite series translate the geometric
concept of proximity into rigorous $\epsilon$-analysis. While in an
incomplete space like $\mathbb{Q}$ a sequence of approximations can
wander into a non-existent gap (such as the rational approximations to
$\sqrt{2}$), completeness guarantees that every sequence whose terms
cluster together (a Cauchy sequence) converges to a definitive real
limit.
